messages.subject: LAVAAN latent code please HELP!!!!
parts:
Hello all, 

I have a question about code specification for latent and composite variables. Taking an example from Jim Grace book, reference below:
Grace, J.B., 2006. Structural Equation Modeling and Natural Systems, 1 edition. ed. Cambridge University Press, Cambridge, UK ; New York.

The codes below are suitable for the models in the pictures?

model_A <- ' 
#Latent to manifest 
soil =~ x1 + x2 +x3
Landscape =~ x4 +x5
Competitors =~ y1
Colonization =~ y2
# regressions
Competitors ~ Soil + Landscape
Colonization ~ Soil + Landscape + Competitors
# Variance / Covariance
Soil ~~Landscape
'


model_B <- ' 
# Manifest to Latent 
soil <~ x1 + x2 +x3 # Lavaan code for composite/formative latent variables
Landscape <~ x4 +x5
Competitors =~ y1
Colonization =~ y2
# regressions
Competitors ~ Soil + Landscape
Colonization ~ Soil + Landscape + Competitors
# Variance / Covariance
Soil ~~Landscape
'
or

model_B <- ' 
# Manifest to Latent 
soil =~ x1 + x2 +x3
Landscape =~ x4 +x5
Competitors =~ y1
Colonization =~ y2
# regressions
Competitors ~ Soil + Landscape
Colonization ~ Soil + Landscape + Competitors
# Variance / Covariance
Soil ~~Landscape
# declaring 0 variance to attempt to formative/composite variables
soil ~~ 0* soil
Landscape ~~ 0*Landscape
'



Model_C <- '
#Latent variables 1 order
true_pH =~ x1
true_moist =~x2
true_texture =~x3
true_dist =~ x4
true_age =~ x5
Competitors =~ y1
Colonization =~ y2
# second orde
soil =~ true_pH + true_moist + true_texture
Landscape =~ true_dist + true_age
# regressions
Competitors ~ Soil + Landscape
Colonization ~ Soil + Landscape + Competitors
'


Or how could I code de below representation blocks (L->M; M->L; M->C blocks)


# L->M block code
model <- '
latent =~ x1+ X2= X3
'

# M-> L block code
model <- '
latent <~ x1+x2+x3
'

# M -> C block code
model <- '
composite =~ x1 + x2 +x3
composite ~~ 0*composite # since composite variables should have zero erro variance


I know that is boring make correction in codes and reply such newbie questions, but I am trying without sucess longer than 2 months. Thus please I need some helping. 

I appreciate any helping
Thanks in advance
Best regards!!

Fernando cesário

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: LAVAAN latent code please HELP!!!!
parts: The codes below are suitable for the models in the pictures?

Model A syntax matches the path diagram.  For Model B, the top syntax matches the path diagram, but not the lower syntax.  Model C syntax does not match the path diagram, for the same reason the lower Model B syntax does not.  The =~ operator specifies arrows pointing from the latent common factor to the indicators, whereas the <~ operator specifies arrows pointing from the "indicators" to the formative construct.  You would also have to fix the (residual) variances of x1-x5 in Model C for the model to be identified.  If you fix them to zero:

x1 ~~ 0*x1

x1 ~~ 0*x1
x1 ~~ 0*x1
x1 ~~ 0*x1
x1 ~~ 0*x1

Then that model would be statistically equivalent to the Model A (if you specify reflective indicators using =~) or Model B (if you specify formative indicators using <~).

Or how could I code de below representation blocks (L->M; M->L; M->C blocks)


# L->M block code
model <- '
latent =~ x1+ X2= X3
'

This is correct, except for a typo.  Use:

latent =~ x1+ x2 + x3

# M-> L block code
model <- '
latent <~ x1+x2+x3
'

This is correct, but not identified because the formative construct does not predict anything else.  Read these for details:

http://dx.doi.org/10.1037/0033-2909.110.2.305

http://dx.doi.org/10.1037/0033-2909.114.3.533

http://dx.doi.org/10.1037/1082-989X.5.2.155

http://dx.doi.org/10.1037/1082-989X.12.2.205

http://dx.doi.org/10.1080/15366367.2015.1016343

http://dx.doi.org/10.1016/j.emj.2016.05.006

http://dx.doi.org/10.1016/j.jom.2016.05.002

# M -> C block code
model <- '
composite =~ x1 + x2 +x3
composite ~~ 0*composite # since composite variables should have zero erro variance

No, this does not match the path diagram.  As noted above, the =~ operator has arrows pointing from the latent, not to the latent.

Terrence D. Jorgensen
Postdoctoral Researcher, Methods and Statistics
Research Institute for Child Development and Education, the University of Amsterdam
UvA web page: http://www.uva.nl/profile/t.d.jorgensen

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: LAVAAN latent code please HELP!!!!
parts: do you have any basic papers about negative variances (Heywood cases) and how fix them?

It is not the negative variance that should be fixed, but the model that produces it (if necessary).  If your model fits poorly, this may be the cause of the negative variance.  You can look at correlation residuals for clues about how your model fails:  

resid(fit, type = "cor")

If your model fits well AND the confidence interval for the Heywood case includes acceptable (positive) values, then there is no evidence that anything besides sampling variability led to the Heywood case, in which case you should just leave it alone.  Forcing a negative variance to be nonnegative will bias other parameter estimates in your model, and it will also merely hide the problem if misfit is the cause.

http://dx.doi.org/10.1037/1082-989X.13.2.150

http://journals.sagepub.com/doi/abs/10.1177/0049124112442138

Terrence D. Jorgensen
Postdoctoral Researcher, Methods and Statistics
Research Institute for Child Development and Education, the University of Amsterdam
UvA web page: http://www.uva.nl/profile/t.d.jorgensen

parts:
Fernando,
  There is no strict rule.  It depends upon your situation.  Rex Kline's book offers some guidance.  One thing that I like to do is to look for outliers in the distribution of correlation residuals.  If the model fits, the distribution should be unimodal around zero.

stem(residuals(fit, type='cor')$cor)

Keith

------------------------
Keith A. Markus
John Jay College of Criminal Justice, CUNY
http://jjcweb.jjay.cuny.edu/kmarkus
Frontiers of Test Validity Theory: Measurement, Causation and Meaning.
